records.label: Index child
quotes: A child presented in early childhood with episodes of coma and hypoglycemia and a rapidly evolutive myopathy and cardiomyopathy leading to death at 9 mo of age.
Ketosis was decreased (blood beta-hydroxybutyrate: 0.07 mmol/L) despite normal plasma levels of fatty acids (0.81 mmol/L).
More specifically, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry identified an accumulation of medium- and long-chain (C8 to C14) 3-hydroxy-dicarboxylic acids

records.label: Five patients with 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria

phenotypes.text: accumulation of 3-hydroxy fatty acids in serum during acute illness
death in infancy at 3 to 14 months
normal long-chain and medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity in fibroblasts

quotes: We describe five patients with a suspected defect in the beta-oxidation of fatty acids characterized by a massive excretion of 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids in the urine and accumulation of 3-hydroxy fatty acids in serum during acute illness.
Four of them died of cardiomyopathy and liver insufficiency at 3 to 14 months of age.
Two of the patients had elder siblings who had died unexpectedly in early infancy.

records.label: Two patients with LCHAD deficiency

phenotypes.text: urinary excretion of even-chain unsubstituted dicarboxylic acids
low long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity in fibroblasts

records.segregation: intermediate enzyme activity in fibroblasts from the parents of one child
quotes: We describe the clinical features and biochemical findings of two patients with long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. Both children presented with an acute metabolic crisis.
Both had hypoglycemia and excreted even-chain unsubstituted dicarboxylic and 3-hydroxy-dicarboxylic acids in the urine.

Measurement of the enzymes of fatty acid oxidation in cultured skin fibroblasts showed low activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, but normal activity of short-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.

records.label: Older sibling
quotes: Two siblings were found to be affected by long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, one of which died suddenly and unexpectedly on the 3rd day of life suffering from extreme hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

records.label: Younger sibling
quotes: The younger sibling started to have feeding problems, lowered consciousness, and liver dysfunction at the age of 5 months. Her urine contained large amounts of C6-C14 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids and conjugated 3-hydroxyoctanoic acid, as verified by gas chromatography/mass spectrometry.
Plasma long-chain acylcarnitine was increased.
Subsequently, the activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase was found to be deficient in cultured skin fibroblasts.

records.label: Young girl with combined enzyme defect

phenotypes.text: severe attack of generalized muscle weakness
accumulation of 3-hydroxyacyl- and 2-enoyl-CoA and carnitine esters and 3-oxoacylcarnitines in muscle mitochondria
low long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity in all tissues
low long-chain 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase activity in muscle mitochondria
low long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase activity in fibroblast, muscle and cardiac mitochondria

records.segregation: Parents' fibroblasts had LCHAD and long-chain thiolase activities intermediate between those of controls and the patient
quotes: A young girl presented with recurrent episodes of muscle weakness culminating in a severe attack of generalized muscle weakness.
There was low activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in mitochondria from all tissues.

The activity of the long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase in fibroblasts from the patient's parents was intermediate between those of controls and the patient.

records.label: Patient with trifunctional protein deficiency

phenotypes.text: deficiency of long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, LCHAD and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase

quotes: a patient which presented with clear manifestations of a mitochondrial beta-oxidation disorder

Subsequent studies in fibroblasts revealed an impairment in palmitate beta-oxidation and in addition, a combined deficiency of long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA-dehydrogenase and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase.

records.label: 11-month-old girl
quotes: An 11-month-old girl presented acute episodes of hypoglycaemia and hepatic encephalopathy reminiscent of Reye syndrome and 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria.
The patient showed peculiar clinical manifestations of severe sensory-motor neuropathy, pigmentary retinopathy, and cardiomyopathy. She died of cardiac failure.

Pathological studies of peripheral nerve showed signs of axonal neuropathy and demyelination. Enzymatic studies in cultured fibroblasts showed a deficiency of mitochondrial long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA-dehydrogenase.

records.label: 6 LCHAD-deficient babies from 5 mothers
quotes: We report on eleven pregnancies in 5 mothers. 6 of the babies had long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl coenzyme A dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency

records.label: 24 unrelated patients expressing only C1528

variants.as_reported: G-->C mutation at nucleotide position 1528 (glutamate to glutamine at position 510)

quotes: Using RFLP, we found that in 24 out of 26 unrelated patients only the C1528 was expressed.
The single base change results in the substitution of a glutamate for a glutamine at amino acid position 510.

records.label: 2 unrelated patients heterozygous for G1528C
quotes: The other two patients were heterozygous for this mutation.

records.label: Patient
quotes: We present a further patient who presented with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, hepatopathy, secondary carnitine deficiency and increased plasma long-chain acylcarnitines.
3-Hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria was present and the diagnosis confirmed in cultured skin fibroblasts.

records.label: Black boy with BRRS and L-CHAD deficiency

phenotypes.text: Deficiency of long-chain L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in cultured skin fibroblasts
Increased size of both lower limbs

quotes: We describe a black boy with findings of BRRS who also has a defect in long-chain fatty acid oxidation expressed in cultured skin fibroblasts as a deficiency of long-chain-L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (L-CHAD).
He also has an abnormal brain MRI and increased size of both lower limbs.

records.label: Infant of mother with AFLP

phenotypes.text: maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy

records.segregation: Mother proved heterozygous for LCHAD deficiency
quotes: We report a woman with acute fatty liver of pregnancy who gave birth to a seemingly normal full-term infant who was seen at 4 mo of age with hypoglycemia, coma and profound hepatic steatosis.
The infant had a defect in fatty acid oxidation, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency, and the mother proved to be heterozygous for this metabolic condition.

records.label: Two affected children homozygous for G1528C
quotes: The analysis in two affected children revealed a G to C mutation at position 1528 (G1528C) of the alpha subunit of the trifunctional protein on both alleles.
This is in the LCHAD domain and substitutes glutamine for glutamic acid at position 474 of mature alpha subunit.
three families with children presenting with sudden unexplained death or hypoglycemia and abnormal liver enzymes (Reye-like syndrome)

records.label: Third child (compound heterozygote)
quotes: The third child had this G1528C mutation on one allele and a different mutation (C1132T) creating a premature termination codon (residue 342) on the second allele.
records.genotype_reason: two different heterozygous variants in one gene

records.label: 34 LCHAD deficient patients
quotes: The finding of an 87% allele frequency of the G1528C mutation in 34 LCHAD deficient patients makes this a valuable test for prenatal diagnosis.

records.label: 13 patients with LCHAD deficiency
records.age_last: one alive at 14 years; others died before 2 years

phenotypes.text: retinopathy with focal pigmentary aggregations or retinal hypopigmentation
bilateral periventricular or focal cortical brain lesions

quotes: We report the clinical findings of 13 patients with long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. At presentation the patients had had hypoglycemia, cardiomyopathy, muscle hypotonia, and hepatomegaly during the first 2 years of life.
All patients were homozygous for the common mutation G1528C.
Only one patient, who has had dietary treatment for 9 years, is alive at the age of 14 years; all others died before they were 2 years of age.

records.label: Two girls with LCHAD deficiency
quotes: The case histories of two girls, aged 8 and 15 years, with LCHAD deficiency are reported.
Both children with LCHAD deficiency exhibited extensive macular pigmentary depositions and a 'salt and pepper' scattering of pigment in their retinas. The patients have decreasing visual acuity.

records.label: Two cases with L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency
quotes: L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: two cases with pigmentary retinopathy.

records.label: 19 children with isolated LCHAD deficiency

variants.as_reported: Glu474Gln with a different mutation in the other allele (11 compound heterozygotes)

records.segregation: 79% of heterozygous mothers carrying fetuses with Glu474Gln had fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome
quotes: Nineteen children had a deficiency only of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver.
In eight children, we identified a homozygous mutation in which glutamic acid at residue 474 was changed to glutamine.
Eleven other children were compound heterozygotes, with this mutation in one allele of the alpha-subunit gene and a different mutation in the other allele.

records.label: 5 children with complete trifunctional protein deficiency
records.segregation: None had Glu474Gln; no mothers had liver disease during pregnancy
quotes: Five other children, who presented with neonatal dilated cardiomyopathy or progressive neuromyopathy, had complete deficiency of the trifunctional protein (loss of activity of all three enzymes). None had the Glu474Gln mutation, and none of their mothers had liver disease during pregnancy.

records.label: Proband
quotes: The proband presented at 2 months of age with an acute infantile hypocalcaemia and vitamin D deficiency associated with occult, unexplained cholestatic liver disease. Sudden, unexpected death occurred at 8 months.
Molecular analysis revealed homozygosity for the prevalent LCHAD (1528G > C, E474Q) mutation.
The mother had pre-eclampsia during the third trimester of her pregnancy.

records.label: Neonate with LCHAD deficiency

phenotypes.text: tachypnoea at first day of life

quotes: Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: neonatal manifestation at the first day of life presenting with tachypnoea.

records.label: 23 patients with proven LCHAD deficiency
quotes: The acylcarnitines in plasma and blood spots of 23 patients with proven deficiency of long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcoenzyme A dehydrogenase were reviewed.

Long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcarnitines of C14:1, C14, C16 and C18:1 chain length, and long-chain acylcarnitines of C12, C14:1, C14, C16, C18:2 and C18:1 chain length were elevated. Acetylcarnitine was decreased.

records.label: 50 LCHAD-deficient patients (questionnaire cohort)
quotes: Questionnaires on 50 patients (82%) were returned and included in this study. The mean age of clinical presentation was 5.8 months (range: 1 day-26 months). Seven (15%) of the patients presented in the neonatal period.

Thirty-nine patients (78%) presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, the classical features of a fatty acid oxidation disorder. Eleven patients (22%) presented with chronic problems, consisting of failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, cholestatic liver disease, and/or hypotonia.

Mortality in this series was high (38%), all dying before or within 3 months after diagnosis. Morbidity in the surviving patients is also high, with recurrent metabolic crises and muscle problems despite therapy.

records.label: 22-month-old child

phenotypes.text: abnormal acylcarnitine pattern on newborn screening

records.segregation: Father heterozygous, mother did not carry the variant; homozygosity was caused by paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2
quotes: We report on a 22-month-old child who was identified on expanded newborn screening with an abnormal acylcarnitine pattern and increased C14OH.
Molecular analysis showed that the child was homozygous for the common mutation, c.1526G > C (p.Glu510Gln) in the HADHA gene.
Carrier testing on the parental samples revealed that the father was heterozygous for the mutation whereas the mother did not carry the mutation.

notes.statement: Guffon et al. (2021) retrospectively analyzed 18 French patients (8 female, 10 male) with long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders, including VLCAD, LCHAD, CACT, CPT II, and MTP deficiencies. The patients were treated with triheptanoin for a median of 22 months (range, 9 to 228 months), and triheptanoin made up 15 to 35% of their daily caloric intake. In the year after starting triheptanoin, 10 of 12 pediatric and 4 of 6 adult patients reported less fatigue and fewer, less severe episodes of myalgia. Three patients no longer had severe hypoglycemic events, and 5 of 6 patients who had needed a wheelchair no longer did.
quotes: Eight female and 10 male patients with LC-FAOD (VLCAD, LCHAD, CACT, CPTII and MTP) were treated with triheptanoin for a median duration of 22 months (range: 9-228 months).
Ten of 12 paediatric patients and 4 of 6 adult patients reported reduced fatigue with reductions in the number and severity of episodes of myalgia.
Of 6 patients, including 1 adult, that had required the use of a wheelchair in the year prior to triheptanoin, all but one no longer required its use.

notes.statement: Guffon et al. (2021) found that emergency hospitalizations decreased after triheptanoin was started, and that no pediatric patient had an emergency hospitalization in the following 12 months. Cumulative annual days of emergency home care fell from 286 to 51. Adverse events were limited to digestive issues that resolved over time, and the authors concluded that long-term triheptanoin treatment appeared safe and improved symptoms.
quotes: The number of emergency hospitalizations decreased, and none were recorded for paediatric patients during these 12 months.
Cumulative annual days of emergency care in the home were reduced from 286 to 51 days in the year before and after initiation, respectively, and 13 patients required no such interventions.
Adverse events were limited to digestive issues that dissipated over time.

notes.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) studied 11 treated patients with LCHAD/TFP deficiency who were on a controlled low-fat diet with MCT. The most prominent fasting long-chain acylcarnitine was C18:1-OH (0.56 +/- 0.52 micromol/L). C16-OH and C18-OH were also above the reference range, and the hydroxyacylcarnitines stayed elevated despite treatment. C18:1-OH fell by 59% after breakfast but rose only 20% after moderate exercise, a smaller and more consistent exercise response than in CPT2 or VLCAD deficiency.
quotes: The most prominent fasting long-chain acylcarnitine was C18:1-OH (0.56 ± 0.52 μmol/L; reference range of 0.00–0.05 μmol/L) (Figure 3A).
C18:1-OH was elevated after an overnight fast, decreased by 59% after breakfast but had minimal change with moderate intensity exercise (Figure 3B).
These ratios were elevated despite treatment when compared to NBS normal ranges (Supplemental Table 1).

notes.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) found that all 9 patients with the common HADHA c.1528G>C (E510Q) mutation on at least one allele had higher levels of C16-OH, C18-OH and C18:1-OH than the 2 patients without it, who had a TFP deficiency phenotype. The difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.09). The authors suggested that mutations that destabilize TFP lower the hydroxyacylcarnitine species because hydratase activity is absent, so the profile looks more like that of VLCAD deficiency.
quotes: All patients with the common mutation (c.1528G>C) in at least one HADHA allele had consistently higher levels of C16-OH, C18-OH and C18:1-OH than the two patients without the common pathogenic variant and a TFP phenotype as previously reported (p = 0.09; Figure 3D).
These findings suggest that mutations that destabilize the protein and result in a loss of mitochondrial TFP expression have low OH-species due to the absence of the hydratase activity.

notes.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) found that plasma acylcarnitines in patients with long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders, including LCHAD deficiency, varied widely through the day: feeding lowered them by about 60%, and exercise raised them. They questioned how useful random outpatient acylcarnitine monitoring is. They recommended standardized sample collection timed to food intake and physical activity. All patients tolerated moderate exercise, which the authors took as support for advising patients to stay physically active.
quotes: The utility of random plasma acylcarnitine analysis for outpatient treatment monitoring may not be beneficial and may not offer useful information beyond the patient’s clinical evaluation.
it is recommended that standardized procedures for sample collection (i.e., timing in relation to food intake and physical activity) are strictly followed to improve their clinical interpretation.
All patients tolerated the exercise further supporting the current recommendations for patients with FAODs to be physically active which could improve long-term fitness and exercise tolerance.

notes.statement: Baskin et al. (2010) found that a child with LCHAD deficiency was homozygous for the common HADHA E510Q mutation. Only the father carried the mutation. Short tandem repeat analysis with markers on both arms of chromosome 2 showed paternal uniparental isodisomy. The authors stressed the importance of testing the parents when a patient with an autosomal recessive disorder is homozygous.
quotes: Short tandem repeat testing with markers covering both short and long arms of chromosome 2 showed that the child has paternal uniparental isodisomy.
We highlight the importance of parental testing in cases of homozygosity in autosomal recessive disorders and its impact on genetic counseling of the family.

notes.statement: Jones et al. (2003) grew cultured skin fibroblasts from LCHAD-deficient and normal individuals in medium containing octanoate, decanoate and palmitate. Adding medium-chain fatty acids reduced the accumulation of long-chain 3-hydroxy fatty acid oxidation intermediates in LCHAD-deficient cells, and decanoate alone worked better than octanoate alone.
quotes: We found that the addition of medium-chain fatty acids caused a decrease in the accumulation of long-chain fatty acid oxidation intermediates in LCHAD-deficient cells when the cells were incubated in untreated medium, and also when they were incubated in this medium with palmitate added.
Medium with decanoate alone was better at achieving this effect than medium with only octanoate added.

notes.statement: Jones et al. (2003) found that a 1:3 ratio of octanoate to decanoate worked best over an extended period in untreated medium, while a 1:1 ratio worked best in medium containing palmitate. They noted that all dietary medium-chain triglyceride preparations contain more octanoate than decanoate, and suggested that a preparation higher in decanoate may be more effective at reducing potentially toxic long-chain 3-hydroxy fatty acids in LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: A 1:3 ratio of octanoate to decanoate worked best over an extended time period in LCHAD-deficient cells in untreated medium, whereas a 1:1 ratio of octanoate to decanoate worked best in the same cells incubated in medium containing palmitate.

Our results suggest that a medium-chain triglyceride preparation that is higher in decanoate may be more effective in reducing the accumulation of potentially toxic long-chain 3-hydroxy-fatty acids in LCHAD deficiency.

notes.statement: To investigate the pathogenesis of pigmentary retinopathy in LCHAD deficiency, Tyni et al. (2002) studied cultured porcine retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells. They found normal chain shortening of [U-13C]-hexadecanoic acid with acetylcarnitine production, LCHAD enzyme activity, expression of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (MTP), and carnitine uptake in these cells.
quotes: Fatty acid oxidation analysis showed normal chain shortening of hexadecanoic acid and production of acetylcarnitine in cultured RPE cells. Immunoblotting revealed expression of the MTP and enzyme assay showed the activity of LCHAD in the RPE cells. RPE cells were also capable of carnitine uptake.

notes.statement: Tyni et al. (2002) detected MTP immunolabeling in the RPE, photoreceptors, and ganglion cells of human retinal sections. They concluded that the findings gave strong in vitro evidence for mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation in RPE cells, but that further studies were needed to determine whether the pathway also operates in the retina in vivo.
quotes: Positive labeling to the MTP antibodies was detected in the RPE, photoreceptors, and ganglion cells.
The results give strong in vitro evidence for the presence of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation in RPE cells and the expression of the MTP in the RPE and other layers of the retina.

notes.statement: In a questionnaire-based review of 50 LCHAD-deficient patients, den Boer et al. (2002) found that 78% presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia and 22% with chronic problems (failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, cholestatic liver disease, and/or hypotonia). In retrospect, 82% of those presenting with acute metabolic derangement had chronic nonspecific symptoms before the crises.
quotes: Thirty-nine patients (78%) presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, the classical features of a fatty acid oxidation disorder.
In retrospect, most (82%) of the patients presenting with an acute metabolic derangement also suffered from a combination of chronic nonspecific symptoms before the metabolic crises.

notes.statement: den Boer et al. (2002) reported 38% mortality, with all deaths occurring before or within 3 months after diagnosis, and concluded that survival can be improved by prompt diagnosis but that morbidity, including recurrent metabolic crises and muscle problems, remained high despite current therapy.
quotes: Mortality in this series was high (38%), all dying before or within 3 months after diagnosis.
Survival can be improved by prompt diagnosis, but morbidity remains alarmingly high despite current therapeutic regimes.

notes.statement: den Boer et al. (2002) described LCHAD deficiency as an autosomal recessive inborn error of fatty acid oxidation.
quotes: LCHAD deficiency is a rare, autosomal recessive inborn error of fatty acid oxidation.

notes.statement: Ibdah et al. (2001) performed molecular prenatal diagnosis in 9 pregnancies: 8 in 6 families with isolated LCHAD deficiency and 1 in a family with complete TFP deficiency. They used chorionic villus samples in 7 pregnancies and amniocytes in 2. The fetal genotype was identified in all 9 pregnancies: 2 fetuses were affected, 2 had a normal genotype, and 5 were heterozygotes. Molecular analysis and enzyme assays on the aborted fetuses and the neonates confirmed these genotypes.
quotes: We performed molecular prenatal diagnosis in 9 pregnancies, 8 in 6 families with isolated long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency and one in a family with complete TFP deficiency.
Molecular prenatal diagnosis successfully identified the fetal genotype in all 9 pregnancies. Two fetuses were affected, and both pregnancies were terminated by family decision.
Genotypes of the aborted fetuses and neonates were confirmed by molecular analysis and enzymatic assays.

notes.statement: Ibdah et al. (2001) found that women heterozygous for TFP alpha-subunit mutations had uncomplicated pregnancies when the fetus was wild-type or heterozygous. All 7 such offspring were alive and apparently healthy.
quotes: Two other fetuses had normal genotype and 5 others were heterozygotes. These 7 pregnancies were uncomplicated, and all the offspring are alive and apparently healthy.
Women heterozygous for TFP alpha-subunit mutations who carry fetuses with wild-type or heterozygous genotypes have uncomplicated pregnancies.

notes.statement: Van Hove et al. (2000) reviewed plasma and blood spot acylcarnitines in 23 patients with LCHAD deficiency and found elevated long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcarnitines (C14:1, C14, C16, C18:1) and long-chain acylcarnitines (C12, C14:1, C14, C16, C18:2, C18:1), with decreased acetylcarnitine.
quotes: Long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcarnitines of C14:1, C14, C16 and C18:1 chain length, and long-chain acylcarnitines of C12, C14:1, C14, C16, C18:2 and C18:1 chain length were elevated. Acetylcarnitine was decreased.

notes.statement: Van Hove et al. (2000) found that in plasma, elevation of hydroxy-C18:1 acylcarnitine above the 95th centile of controls combined with elevation of 2 of the 3 acylcarnitines C14, C14:1, and hydroxy-C16 identified over 85% of LCHAD-deficient patients with less than 0.1% false positives. Blood spots had lower specificity because of high endogenous long-chain acylcarnitines in normal erythrocytes; results were diagnostic in asymptomatic patients and not influenced by genotype.
quotes: In plasma, elevation of hydroxy-C18:1 acylcarnitine over the 95th centile of controls, in combination with an elevation of two of the three acylcarnitines C14, C14:1 and hydroxy-C16, identified over 85% of patients with high specificity (less than 0.1% false positive rate).
High endogenous levels of long-chain acylcarnitines in normal erythrocytes reduced the diagnostic specificity in blood spots compared with plasma samples.
The results were also diagnostic in asymptomatic patients, and were not influenced by genotype.

notes.statement: Van Hove et al. (2000) found that treatment with a diet low in fat and high in medium-chain triglycerides decreased all disease-specific acylcarnitines, often to normal, suggesting that the assay is useful for treatment monitoring.
quotes: Treatment with diet low in fat and high in medium-chain triglyceride decreased all disease-specific acylcarnitines, often to normal, suggesting that this assay is useful in treatment monitoring.

notes.statement: Carpenter and Wilcken (1999) reported the neonatal diagnosis of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency and discussed what it means for newborn screening by tandem mass spectrometry.
quotes: Neonatal diagnosis of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency and implications for newborn screening by tandem mass spectrometry.

notes.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) reported that the mother of an LCHAD-deficient infant had preeclampsia in the third trimester of that pregnancy and, in a subsequent pregnancy, developed severe acute fatty liver of pregnancy with intrauterine fetal death at 33 weeks' gestation. They concluded that fetal LCHAD deficiency is associated with a spectrum of maternal illness ranging from preeclampsia to life-threatening AFLP.
quotes: In a subsequent pregnancy, she developed severe acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP) and intrauterine fetal death at 33 weeks of gestation.
The maternal pregnancy history documents that fetal LCHAD deficiency is associated with a spectrum of maternal illnesses ranging from pre-eclampsia to life-threatening AFLP.

notes.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) found that 79% of heterozygous mothers carrying fetuses with the Glu474Gln mutation had acute fatty liver of pregnancy or the HELLP syndrome during those pregnancies. None of the mothers of 5 children with complete trifunctional protein deficiency and no Glu474Gln mutation had liver disease during pregnancy.
quotes: While carrying fetuses with the Glu474Gln mutation, 79 percent of the heterozygous mothers had fatty liver of pregnancy or the HELLP syndrome.
None had the Glu474Gln mutation, and none of their mothers had liver disease during pregnancy.

notes.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) studied 24 children with 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. The 19 with isolated LCHAD deficiency had hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver and carried the Glu474Gln mutation in 1 or both alleles. The 5 with complete trifunctional protein deficiency had neonatal dilated cardiomyopathy or progressive neuromyopathy and did not carry Glu474Gln. The authors concluded that women with acute liver disease during pregnancy may carry a Glu474Gln mutation and that their infants are at risk for hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver.
quotes: In 24 children with 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, we used DNA amplification and nucleotide-sequence analyses to identify mutations in the alpha subunit of the trifunctional protein.
Women with acute liver disease during pregnancy may have a Glu474Gln mutation in long-chain hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase. Their infants are at risk for hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver.

notes.statement: Schrijver-Wieling et al. (1997) recommended that testing for LCHAD deficiency be included in the diagnostic evaluation of children with retinal dystrophy, particularly when other clinical symptoms have occurred, noting that patients tend to be symptom-free between attacks.
quotes: Testing for the disorder, therefore, should be included in the diagnostic process for children with retinal dystrophy, in particular when other clinical symptoms are known to have occurred.

notes.statement: Schrijver-Wieling et al. (1997) stated that early recognition of LCHAD deficiency can increase life expectancy through avoidance of catabolism and appropriate diets.
quotes: The early recognition of LCHAD deficiency can increase the life expectancy in these patients through avoiding catabolism and through appropriate diets.

notes.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) found that in skin fibroblasts from LCHAD-deficient patients homozygous for G1528C, the enoyl-CoA hydratase and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activities of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein were variably decreased.
quotes: However, the enoyl-CoA hydratase and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activities of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein were variably decreased in skin fibroblasts.

notes.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) noted that the only surviving patient of 13 had received dietary treatment for 9 years and was alive at 14 years, and emphasized that early recognition allows dietary management that may alter the otherwise invariably poor prognosis.
quotes: Recognition of the clinical features of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA deficiency is important for the early institution of dietary management, which may alter the otherwise invariably poor prognosis.

notes.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) noted that cholestatic liver disease, seen in 2 of their 13 patients, is uncommon in beta-oxidation defects; 7 patients had recurrent metabolic crises and 6 had a steadily progressive course.
quotes: Seven patients had recurrent metabolic crises, and six patients had a steadily progressive course. Two patients had cholestatic liver disease, which is uncommon in beta-oxidation defects.

notes.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) expressed wildtype and mutant MTP alpha subunit in S. cerevisiae and showed that the G1528C missense mutation was directly responsible for the loss of LCHAD activity.
quotes: Using S. cerevisiae for expression of wild type and mutant protein we show that the G1528C mutation is directly responsible for the loss of LCHAD activity.

notes.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) found the G1528C mutation at an allele frequency of 87% in 34 patients with LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: The finding of an 87% allele frequency of the G1528C mutation in 34 LCHAD deficient patients makes this a valuable test for prenatal diagnosis.

notes.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) developed a method to identify the G1528C mutation in genomic DNA. Because the mutation is so common, they proposed it as a useful test for prenatal diagnosis.
quotes: Furthermore, we describe a newly developed method allowing identification of the G1528C mutation in genomic DNA.
The finding of an 87% allele frequency of the G1528C mutation in 34 LCHAD deficient patients makes this a valuable test for prenatal diagnosis.

notes.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) mapped the gene encoding the MTP alpha subunit to chromosome 2p24.1-p23.3.
quotes: Finally, we show that the gene encoding the alpha subunit of MTP is located on chromosome 2p24.1-23.3.

notes.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) noted that most patients have deficient LCHAD activity of MTP alone, while the long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase and long-chain 3-ketothiolase activities are near normal.
quotes: In most patients only the LCHAD activity of MTP is deficient with near normal activity of the two other enzyme activities of the complex.

notes.statement: Treem et al. (1994) hypothesized that some cases of acute fatty liver of pregnancy result from the interaction of a fetus affected with LCHAD deficiency and a mother heterozygous for the defect in the late third trimester.
quotes: We hypothesize that the interaction of an affected fetus with a female heterozygous for this defect in fatty acid oxidation in the late third trimester accounts for some cases of acute fatty liver of pregnancy.

notes.statement: Wilcken et al. (1993) reported 11 pregnancies in 5 mothers; all 6 pregnancies with an LCHAD-deficient fetus were complicated by features such as maternal acute fatty liver and HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets) syndrome, whereas pregnancies with unaffected babies in 3 of the mothers were largely uncomplicated.
quotes: 6 of the babies had long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl coenzyme A dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency, and each of the pregnancies was complicated by features such as fatty liver and HELLP (haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets) syndrome.
By contrast, 3 of the mothers also gave birth to unaffected babies, and these pregnancies were largely uncomplicated.

notes.statement: Wilcken et al. (1993) concluded that a fetus with LCHAD deficiency may have adverse effects on maternal liver function, and that maternal heterozygosity alone cannot account for these effects because they segregated with fetal LCHAD status.
quotes: We conclude that there may be adverse effects on maternal liver function from a fetus with LCHAD deficiency.
Heterozygosity in the mother cannot alone account for the adverse effects because of the segregation of these effects with fetal LCHAD status.

notes.statement: Fryburg et al. (1994) proposed that L-CHAD deficiency might cause the lipid storage myopathy seen in Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome. They based this on a boy who had BRRS together with L-CHAD deficiency in cultured fibroblasts.
quotes: The etiology of the lipid storage myopathy has been unclear.
postulate that L-CHAD deficiency may be the cause of the lipid myopathy in BRRS.

notes.statement: Sims et al. (1995) reported 3 families with children with LCHAD deficiency presenting with sudden unexplained death or hypoglycemia and abnormal liver enzymes (Reye-like syndrome); in all families the mothers had acute fatty liver and associated severe complications during pregnancies with the affected infants.
quotes: three families with children presenting with sudden unexplained death or hypoglycemia and abnormal liver enzymes (Reye-like syndrome)
In all families, the mothers had acute fatty liver and associated sever complications during pregnancies with the affected infants.

notes.statement: Using SSCP analysis of the exons of the trifunctional protein alpha subunit gene, Sims et al. (1995) identified a G1528C (glu474-to-gln) mutation in the LCHAD domain in homozygous state in 2 affected children and in compound heterozygosity with a C1132T nonsense mutation (premature termination at residue 342) in a third, concluding that mutations in the LCHAD domain in affected offspring are associated with maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy. This was the initial delineation of the molecular basis of isolated LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: Our results demonstrate that mutations in the LCHAD domain of the trifunctional protein alpha subunit in affected offspring are associated with maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy.
This is the initial delineation of the molecular basis of isolated LCHAD deficiency.

notes.statement: Sewell et al. (1994) described 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency as a newly recognized fatty acid oxidation disorder with a usually fatal outcome.
quotes: 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is a newly recognised fatty acid oxidation disorder with a usually fatal outcome.

notes.statement: IJlst et al. (1994) sequenced cDNAs encoding the alpha and beta subunits of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein in patients with LCHAD deficiency. They found a G-to-C change at nucleotide 1528 in the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase coding region of the alpha subunit, which caused a glu510-to-gln substitution and created a PstI site. Using RFLP analysis, they found that 24 of 26 unrelated patients expressed only C1528 and the other 2 were heterozygous.
quotes: we sequenced the cDNAs encoding the alpha- and beta-subunits which revealed one G-->C mutation at nucleotide position 1528 in the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase encoding region of the alpha-subunit.
The base substitution creates a PstI restriction site.
Using RFLP, we found that in 24 out of 26 unrelated patients only the C1528 was expressed.

notes.statement: IJlst et al. (1994) did not find the G1528C mutation in 55 control subjects. They concluded that the mutation was highly frequent among patients with LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: This mutation was not found in 55 different control subjects. This indicates a high frequency for this mutation in long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficient patients.

notes.statement: Wanders et al. (1989) discussed long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in relation to sudden infant death.
quotes: Sudden infant death and long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.

notes.statement: Hagenfeldt et al. (1990) found that fibroblasts from 5 patients with 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria had normal long-chain and medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activities. The authors concluded that these patients differed from previously described patients with beta-oxidation defects.
quotes: Long-chain and medium-chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenases in fibroblasts were normal in all patients.
These patients differ from previously described patients with beta-oxidation defects.

notes.statement: Rocchiccioli et al. (1990) found impaired medium- and long-chain fatty acid oxidation and deficiency of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in the patient's cultured fibroblasts, whereas activities of long-, medium-, and short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase were normal.
quotes: Biochemical studies in the patient's cultured fibroblasts confirmed the impairment of medium- and long-chain fatty acid oxidation, and allowed the recognition of the deficiency of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
The activities of long-, medium-, and short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase were normal.

notes.statement: Rocchiccioli et al. (1990) noted that LCHAD deficiency shares clinical similarities with systemic carnitine deficiency and CPT and LCAD deficiencies, and that differential diagnosis relies on demonstrating long-chain urinary 3-hydroxy-dicarboxylic acids and measuring enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts.
quotes: It is important to point out that long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA deficiency shares many clinical similarities with systemic carnitine deficiency, as well as with carnitine-palmityl-CoA transferase and long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiencies.

The differential diagnosis of this disease relies on the demonstration of long-chain urinary dicarboxylic acids with a hydroxyl group in 3-position and the study of the enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts.

notes.statement: Duran et al. (1991) found that a phenylpropionic acid loading test gave a clue to the diagnosis of LCHAD deficiency. The test showed small but significant amounts of conjugated 3-hydroxyphenylpropionic acid (phenylhydracrylic acid) in the patient's urine. Deficient LCHAD activity was then shown in cultured skin fibroblasts.
quotes: A clue to the diagnosis was given by the results of a phenylpropionic acid loading test. This revealed small, but significant amounts of conjugated 3-hydroxyphenylpropionic acid (phenylhydracrylic acid) in the patient's urine.

notes.statement: Duran et al. (1991) prescribed a diet enriched in medium-chain triglycerides, based on the results of a medium-chain triglyceride load. On this diet, the LCHAD-deficient patient began to thrive, signs of cardiomyopathy disappeared, and liver function returned to normal.
quotes: Based on the findings obtained by a medium-chain triglyceride load, a diet enriched in this type of fat was prescribed. On this regimen the patient started to thrive, signs of cardiomyopathy disappeared, and her liver function normalized.

notes.statement: Jackson et al. (1991) found low long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity but normal short-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity in cultured skin fibroblasts from 2 patients. They characterized the defect further by immunoprecipitating the short-chain enzyme with monospecific antibodies.
quotes: Measurement of the enzymes of fatty acid oxidation in cultured skin fibroblasts showed low activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, but normal activity of short-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
The defect was further characterized by immunoprecipitating the short-chain enzyme using monospecific antibodies.

notes.statement: Jackson et al. (1991) concluded that LCHAD deficiency is probably inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, because fibroblasts from the parents of one affected child showed intermediate enzyme activity.
quotes: It is probably inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, inasmuch as intermediate enzyme activity was found in the fibroblasts from the parents of one child.

notes.statement: Bertini et al. (1992) noted that peripheral nerve involvement and retinal pigmentary degeneration had not previously been described in patients with proven defects of mitochondrial beta-oxidation.
quotes: Peripheral nerve involvement and retinal pigmentary degeneration have as yet not been described in patients with proven defects of mitochondrial beta-oxidation.

notes.statement: Wanders et al. (1992) used size-exclusion chromatography to show that a patient's fibroblasts lacked the membrane-bound multifunctional beta-oxidation enzyme protein. This explained the patient's combined deficiency of long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase. The authors described this as a new disorder, trifunctional protein deficiency.
quotes: We show by means of size-exclusion chromatography that there is, indeed, a deficiency of the multifunctional beta-oxidation enzyme protein in this patient.
The recent identification of a multifunctional, membrane-bound beta-oxidation enzyme protein catalyzing all these three enzyme activities

notes.statement: Jackson et al. (1992) found that their patient's long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase activity was low in fibroblast, muscle and cardiac mitochondria when measured with 3-oxohexadecanoyl-CoA. With 3-oxooctanoyl-CoA as the substrate, the deficiency was only partial.
quotes: 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase activity measured with 3-oxohexadecanoyl-CoA as substrate was low in fibroblast, muscle, and cardiac mitochondria but only partial deficiency was present when the activity was measured with 3-oxooctanoyl-CoA

notes.statement: Jackson et al. (1992) concluded that their patient had a combined defect of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase and long-chain 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase, apparently inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. They suggested that a single multifunctional enzyme catalyzes these activities in human mitochondria and that this enzyme was deficient in the patient.
quotes: The patient has a combined defect of the long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase, and long-chain 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase which appears to be inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
This suggests there is a multifunctional enzyme catalyzing these activities in human mitochondria and that this enzyme is deficient in our patient.
